title: Coinduced discrete modules are acyclic in positive continuous cohomology
statement: Using [def-exc-continuous-cohomology], let $G$ be a profinite group, $\ell$ a prime, and $M$ a discrete continuous $\ell$-primary $G$-module. Let $\operatorname{Cont}(G,M)$ be the abelian group of continuous functions $G\to M$, with the coinduced action $(g\cdot f)(x)=f(xg)$ by right translation. Then $\operatorname{Cont}(G,M)$ is again discrete, continuous, and $\ell$-primary; the map $M\to\operatorname{Cont}(G,M)$, $m\mapsto(x\mapsto xm)$, is $G$-equivariant; and $H^q(G,\operatorname{Cont}(G,M))=0$ for every $q\geq1$. The vanishing is given by the standard contracting homotopy on continuous homogeneous cochains.

proof.text: Module structure. Cont(G,M) is an abelian group (an A-module if M is one) under pointwise operations, and right translation is an action by additive automorphisms. Discreteness: for f in Cont(G,M), [lem-exc-coinduced-functions-open-stabilizer] applied to f (M discrete) gives an open normal subgroup U with f(xu)=f(x) for all x and u in U, i.e. u.f=f, so the stabilizer of f is open. ell-primary: f is continuous from compact G to discrete M, so it takes finitely many values, each killed by a power of ell; hence f is killed by the largest of these powers. Equivariance: for m in M and g in G, (g.(x -> xm))(x)=xgm, which is the image of gm. The map x -> xm lies in Cont(G,M) because it is constant on left cosets x Stab(m) of the open stabilizer of m.

source.place: proof, third paragraph: the continuous cochain complex of a coinduced module is contractible in positive degrees

proof.text: For n>=1 and a continuous inhomogeneous n-cochain F with values in Cont(G,M), define h_n(F)(g_1,...,g_{n-1})(x)=F(x,g_1,...,g_{n-1})(1). Evaluation at 1 and substitution are A-linear. The resulting function is continuous: for each fixed tuple, continuity of F and discreteness of M give open neighborhoods on which the evaluated value is constant, and compactness of G supplies a finite subcover whose intersection works uniformly in x; the open-normal invariance statement [lem-exc-coinduced-functions-open-stabilizer] supplies the corresponding discrete continuity condition. Thus h_nF is a continuous (n-1)-cochain.

source.place: proof, third paragraph: the continuous cochain complex of a coinduced module is contractible in positive degrees

proof.text: Substitute the displayed formula for h into the inhomogeneous differential. At (g_1,...,g_n) and x, the expansion of d^{n-1}h_nF has the terms F(xg_1,g_2,...,g_n)(1), the alternating interior product terms, and the final term (-1)^n F(x,g_1,...,g_{n-1})(1). The expansion of h_{n+1}d^nF has the term F(g_1,...,g_n)(x), the same translated and interior terms with opposite signs, and the endpoint term (-1)^{n+1}F(x,g_1,...,g_{n-1})(1). Hence all terms except F(g_1,...,g_n)(x) cancel, giving d^{n-1}h_nF+h_{n+1}d^nF=F.

source.place: proof, third paragraph: standard contracting homotopy on continuous homogeneous cochains

proof.text: If q>=1 and F is a q-cocycle, then d^qF=0. The identity in the preceding step gives F=d^{q-1}(h_qF), so F is a coboundary. Therefore the q-th continuous cohomology vanishes for every q>=1.
